english.note: Use this colloquial intensifier before an adjective when “wildly” means extremely, as in “wildly exaggerated.”
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that someone or something is extremely or incredibly so.
Use 勁 as the all-purpose colloquial intensifier for an unusually high degree, especially with adjectives such as 快.
Use this colloquial intensifier in speech, especially before an adjective such as 勁快 or 勁好.
Use this colloquial intensifier for a stronger, more emphatic tone in casual speech.
Use this more emphatic colloquial choice when the speaker wants to stress an exceptionally high degree.
Use this colloquial intensifier when emphasizing that an adjective applies to a very high degree.
Use this colloquial intensifier before an adjective or verb when the extraordinary degree is emphatic and conversational.
Use this colloquial intensifier when the degree is striking or impressive.
Use this colloquial intensifier before an adjective when the meaning is ‘extremely’.
Use this colloquial intensifier for a punchier, more emphatic tone, especially before adjectives or stative predicates.
Use this colloquial intensifier for especially emphatic statements, often about strong feelings or reactions.
Use this casual intensifier when the meaning is roughly really or damn, especially with energetic or impressive descriptions.
